title: Unique Combination Sum
statement:
List every distinct combination of numbers that adds up to a target when each number may be used at most once.

Contract
- `candidates` holds positive integers, may repeat, and may be empty. `target` is positive.
- Each element of `candidates` (each position) may be used at most once, so a value that appears twice can be used at most twice.
- Return every combination whose sum is exactly `target`. Combinations are multisets: report each distinct combination once, even if it can be formed from different positions.
- The order of the combinations and of the numbers inside each combination do not matter. Return an empty list when nothing reaches the target. Do not mutate `candidates`.

Examples
- `combinations(new int[]{4, 1, 1, 2, 3}, 5)` returns `[[1, 1, 3], [1, 4], [2, 3]]` in any order.
- `combinations(new int[]{2, 2, 2}, 4)` returns `[[2, 2]]`.
- `combinations(new int[]{3, 5}, 4)` returns `[]`.
hints: Build a combination one number at a time and track how much of the target is still missing. Each position can be used only once, so after choosing a number move on to later positions.

Sort the candidates so that equal numbers are adjacent and so a branch can stop once a number exceeds the remainder. Among alternatives for the same slot, never start a branch from a value equal to one already tried in that loop, which prevents repeated combinations.

Alternatively group the sorted values into (value, count) pairs and decide how many copies, from none up to the count, to take of each value. The probe uses n equal values with a target of n / 2, which has a single answer. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for that family; in general the number of combinations is exponential.
inputSyntax: Input: the candidates followed by the target, for example: [4, 1, 1, 2, 3] 5
